summary: Hyoung Seok Ham specializes in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Virginia in 2010 and earned his PhD at the University of Michigan, supervised by Madhav M. Deshpande alongside other teachers.

Hürelbaatar Ujeed specializes in religious, Buddhist, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He earned a Ph.D. in Social Anthropology from the University of Cambridge, later holding posts there and as Professor at Inner Mongolia University for Nationalities.
Hōkai was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Hōgetsu and Zuihe.
Hōkei Izumi was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Otani University and served there as a professor from circa 1921 to 1947.

Ian Charles Harris was a Buddhist and religious studies scholar. He studied at Cambridge and Lancaster, served at the University of Cumbria (~1986–2014) as Professor Emeritus, and held positions at Oxford, NUS, and Lancaster.
Ian James Coghlan specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He completed a doctorate in Asian Studies at La Trobe University in 2004 and served as a research fellow at Monash University.
Ian Kishizawa was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Saitama University and under traditional teacher Sotan Oka, and later taught Shunryu Suzuki.

Ian Reader is a scholar of Japanology and religious studies who earned his doctorate from the University of Leeds. He held posts at Kansai Gaidai, Kobe University of Commerce, the University of Stirling, and the University of Hawaii.
Ibrahim Shah is an archaeology scholar who earned his PhD from the University of Peshawar in 2007 under Muhammad Farooq Swati. He became Associate Professor and Chairman at Hazara University.

Ichijo Ogawa is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Otani University (~1955–1959) and held positions at Otani University Junior College (~1964–1978) and Otani University (~1968–2007).

Ichiro Hori was a religious studies and archaeology scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo. He held posts at Kokugakuin University, Tohoku University, the University of Tokyo, Seijo University, and Nishogakusha University.
Ichiro Katayama is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Komazawa University from circa 1960 to 1965 and served there as a professor from circa 1986 to 2013.
Ignazio Guidi was an Italian scholar of linguistics and history/archaeology. He studied at the Sapienza University of Rome (~1864–1869) and later held a post there from circa 1876 to 1920.

Igor Dmitrievich Serebryakov was an Indology and linguistics scholar educated at Saint Petersburg State University (~1936–1941). He served at the Military Institute of Foreign Languages, Pravda, and the Institute of Oriental Studies (~1960–1998).
Ikko Arai is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD from Komazawa University. He studied under Shiro Matsumoto, Kazunobu Matsuda, Lambert Schmithausen, Harunaga Isaacson, and Michael Zimmermann.
Ikuhisa Takigawa is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Waseda University and served as a part-time lecturer at both Waseda University and Tokai University.
Ikuko Tazaki is a researcher in Buddhist and religious studies who has held research posts at Otani University and Kyoto University.

Ilkka Pyysiäinen is a religious studies scholar who completed his PhD at the University of Helsinki under René Gothóni. He held posts at the University of Helsinki and as a visiting researcher at the University of Oxford.
Imre Galambos is a scholar of Sinology and Tibetology. He studied at Eötvös Loránd, Nankai, and UC Berkeley (PhD), later holding posts at the British Library and the University of Cambridge.

Imre Hamar is a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies who studied at Eötvös Loránd University and National Taiwan Normal University. He has served as a professor at Eötvös Loránd University and visited Otani University.
